{{Short description|Mathematical Graph}}
In [[graph theory]], a '''walk-regular graph''' is a [[simple graph]] where the number of closed walks of any length <math>\ell</math> from a vertex to itself does only depend on <math>\ell</math> but not depend on the choice of vertex.<ref name="DFG2008">{{cite journal |last1=Dalfó |first1=C. |last2=Fiol |first2=M.A. |last3=Garriga |first3=E. |title=On k-Walk-Regular Graphs |journal=Electronic Journal of Combinatorics |date=2009 |volume=16 |issue=1 |pages=#R47 |doi=10.37236/136 |doi-access=free|url=https://upcommons.upc.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/feeffccf-e0d3-4980-a811-ea2314c1b31b/content }}</ref> Walk-regular graphs can be thought of as a [[spectral graph theory]] analogue of [[vertex-transitive graph]]s.
While a walk-regular graph is not necessarily very [[graph automorphism|symmetric]], all its vertices still behave identically with respect to the graph's spectral properties.

== Equivalent definitions ==
Suppose that <math>G</math> is a simple graph. Let <math>A</math> denote the [[adjacency matrix]] of <math>G</math>, <math>V(G)</math> denote the set of vertices of <math>G</math>, and <math>\Phi_{G - v}(x)</math> denote the characteristic polynomial of the vertex-deleted subgraph <math>G - v</math> for all <math>v \in V(G).</math>Then the following are equivalent:
* <math>G</math> is walk-regular.
* <math>A^k</math> is a constant-diagonal matrix for all <math>k \geq 0.</math>
* <math>\Phi_{G - u}(x) = \Phi_{G - v}(x)</math> for all <math>u, v \in V(G).</math>

== Examples ==
* The [[vertex-transitive graph]]s are walk-regular.<ref name="BrouwerHaemers2012"/>
* The [[distance-regular graph]]s are walk-regular.<ref name="DFG2008"/> More generally, any simple graph in a homogeneous [[coherent algebra]] is walk-regular.
* A connected [[regular graph]] is walk-regular if it has at most four distinct [[eigenvalue]]s.<ref name="BrouwerHaemers2012">{{citation |last1=Brouwer |first1=Andries E. |last2=Haemers |first2=Willem H. |title=Spectra of Graphs |chapter=Graphs with few eigenvalues |series=Universitext |publisher=Springer |location=New York, NY |year=2012 |isbn=978-1-4614-1939-6 |doi=10.1007/978-1-4614-1939-6 |pages=217–218 |url=https://aeb.win.tue.nl/2WF02/spectra.pdf}}</ref>

== Properties ==
* A walk-regular graph is necessarily a regular graph, since the number of closed walks of length two starting at any vertex is twice the vertex's degree.<ref name="DFG2008"/>
* [[Graph complement|Complements]] of walk-regular graphs are walk-regular. <ref name = "GodsilMcKay">{{cite journal |last1=Godsil |first1=C.D. |last2=McKay |first2=B.D. |title=Feasibility conditions for the existence of walk-regular graphs |journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications |date=April 1980 |volume=30 |pages=51–61 |doi=10.1016/0024-3795(80)90180-9 }}</ref>
* [[Cartesian product of graphs|Cartesian products]] of walk-regular graphs are walk-regular.<ref name = "GodsilMcKay"/>
* [[Tensor product of graphs|Categorical products]] of walk-regular graphs are walk-regular.<ref name = "GodsilMcKay"/>
* [[Strong product of graphs|Strong products]] of walk-regular graphs are walk-regular. <ref name = "GodsilMcKay"/>
* In general, the [[line graph]] of a walk-regular graph is not walk-regular.

== ''k''-walk-regular graphs ==

A graph is '''<math>k</math>-walk-regular''' if for any two vertices <math>v</math> and <math>w</math> of [[distance (graph theory)|distance]] at most <math>k,</math> the number of walks of length <math>\ell</math>  from <math>v</math> to <math>w</math> depends only on <math>k</math> and <math>\ell</math>.<ref name="DFG2008"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dalfó |first1=C. |last2=Fiol |first2=M.A. |last3=Garriga |first3=E. |title=On t-Cliques in k-Walk-Regular Graphs |journal=Electronic Notes in Discrete Mathematics |date=August 2009 |volume=34 |pages=579–584 |doi=10.1016/j.endm.2009.07.096 |hdl=2117/10784 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

The class of <math>0</math>-walk-regular graphs is exactly the class of walk-regular graphs

In analogy to walk-regular graphs generalizing vertex-transitive graphs, 1-walk-regular graphs can be thought of as generalizing [[symmetric graph]]s, that is, graphs that are both vertex- and edge-transitive. For example, the [[Hoffman graph]] is 1-walk-regular but not symmetric.

If <math>k</math> is at least the [[diameter (graph theory)|diameter]] of the graph, then the <math>k</math>-walk-regular graphs coincide with the [[distance-regular graphs]].
In fact, if <math>k\ge 2</math> and the graph has an eigenvalue of multiplicity at most <math>k</math> (except for eigenvalues <math>d</math> and <math>-d</math>, where <math>d</math> is the [[degree (graph theory)|degree]] of the graph), then the graph is already distance-regular.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cámara |first1=Marc |last2=van Dam |first2=Edwin R. |last3=Koolen |first3=Jack H. |last4=Park |first4=Jongyook |title=Geometric aspects of 2-walk-regular graphs |journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications |date=November 2013 |volume=439 |issue=9 |pages=2692–2710 |doi=10.1016/j.laa.2013.07.028 |arxiv=1304.2905 }}</ref>
